title: The control rules get a row for a control that can only act over part of its range
goal: The written rules have one settled ladder for a control that cannot act at all: a command dims, a chooser is replaced by the answer, a field keeps its number read only, a bare handle is removed, a key press speaks on the canvas. There is no row for the control that keeps turning up: one that works fine, but only across part of its range, or that is offered over something it barely reaches. Four surfaces hit it in the last week and each invented its own answer, so this unblocks the focus directly: a-slider-says-where-its-track-starts-when-someth and a-measurement-offers-a-corner-radius-it-has-noth are both waiting to be told what the row should say, and the icon frames work keeps running into it too.
notes:
Found by the 2026-09-12 design review. Evidence: queue/audits/2026-09-12-corner-over-a-group.json, both of its last two rough notes, where Corner Radius over a group has a floor of 18 that only a tooltip explains, and a pill's slider switches itself off silently.

The existing rule is UX-PATTERNS.md section 4, "A control that cannot act", written 2026-09-04 after six fixes answered the same question six ways. It is a good rule and it holds; it just stops one row short. Its own field row already settles the look of a number you cannot type and says "Never a hover tip alone", so the shape of the answer is there to follow.

This serves the design-system epic, which is staged next, so it sits at p3 rather than taking a place ahead of focus work. The concrete case is fixed under a-slider-says-where-its-track-starts-when-someth at p2 without waiting for this.
acceptance: UX-PATTERNS section 4 gains a row for a control whose range is clamped by something else, saying what it must show without the pointer on it
The rule cites the case it was taken from and the audit it came out of
The audit gates in section 9 gain the matching check
No behaviour changes in this task; anything the new rule names as already wrong is filed rather than quietly fixed

The rule answers all four cases found so far: Corner Radius over a group whose contents are rounded 18 (a floor), Corner Radius on a pill with nothing left to round, Corner Radius on a measurement with no corners at all, and Border Width running 0 to 20 on a 24 pixel icon frame where only the first few steps mean anything
a-slider-says-where-its-track-starts-when-someth and a-measurement-offers-a-corner-radius-it-has-noth can both be built straight from the rule without inventing anything on the row

log.note: DESIGN REVIEW 2026-09-14: moved p3 to p2. It was sitting below the four p2 tasks that are waiting on its answer, which is backwards: a-slider-says-where-its-track-starts-when-someth says in its own acceptance that the answer must be drawn from the UX-PATTERNS section 4 rule rather than invented on the row, and that rule has no row for this case. Fourth instance found today: the Border Width slider still runs 0 to 20 on a 24 pixel icon frame, where only the first few steps mean anything (audit queue/audits/2026-09-14-icon-stroke-weight.json, fourth rough item).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before writing. The mock-and-audit evidence pointed at one answer (a clamped slider needs a marker) and that answer is wrong for two of the four cases, so the rule leads with sorting rather than with drawing. (a) A measurement's Corner Radius is not clamped at all: there is no true number at any value, so it is the ladder's existing field row and the answer is no row. Treating it as clamped would have put a spent track on a control nothing is refusing. (b) Border Width 0 to 20 on a 24 pixel icon is not clamped either: every value is reachable and does what it says. The icon audit already measured it at about 205 points of track, so one point of width is about 10 points of travel, which is a comfortable target, and the rule's answer there is LEAVE IT ALONE. Decorating it would have been pure noise. (c) The group audit's own third rough note records trying to remove the row and calls it the mistake, so 'take it away' is ruled out by evidence rather than by taste. Only two of the four cases are actually this rule.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, after drawing. First specimen build used the page's default slrow and a 20 percent ink wash: at 64 points of track you could not see the thing the specimen exists to show, and the wash was too faint to tell from the empty groove. Rebuilt with .slrow.stack (200 points of track) and the spent stretch drawn as a SOLID neutral segment rather than a wash, so a clamped slider reads as three materials left to right: given, yours, empty. Verified in the browser at 127.0.0.1:8791 in both themes, no console errors, and the measured geometry agrees with the rule (wall at 60.4 of 200, fill 0.2 wide at the wall, 62.1 when pulled past, 200 when spent end to end).

left rough: comp-sliders block 03 still opens 'Four, each solving a problem the plain slider gets wrong', and .clamped is arguably a fifth. It sits in its own block 05 with its own name, so nothing is mislabelled, and rewording a specimen intro is not something a person would notice. Not filed.

left rough: the comp-sliders page intro carries an em dash ('the variants a photo editor actually needs — a fill that grows'), which the copy rule forbids. Pre-existing, not mine, and a wording nit in a specimen intro rather than something a person is stopped by. Not filed.
No sweep requested: this task changed no app code and no walk, only docs, mock CSS and one mock page. Scripts/test.sh run anyway per the repo rule: 6534 tests in 531 suites, all passing, 79s.

Epic check: this serves design-system, staged 'next' rather than 'now'. Kept rather than dropped because two OPEN tasks were explicitly waiting on it (a-slider-says-where-its-track-starts-when-someth, whose own acceptance says the answer must come from this rule rather than be invented, and a-measurement-offers-a-corner-radius-it-has-noth), and both serve epics staged now. That is the 'foundational work earns its place by unblocking the feature in focus' case, and the goal already named it.

UX-PATTERNS section 4 gains 'A control that can only act over part of its range' (doc to v1.9), a 0b gate before the cannot-act ladder, a row in the ladder's table, and an audit gate in section 9. It sorts the three lookalikes (nothing to act on gets no row, a range merely wider than the subject gets nothing, only a clamped range gets the treatment) and answers all four cases it was written from, each cited to its audit. Drawn as .slider.clamped in shared/components/slider.css with a three-state specimen at pages/comp-sliders.html block 05, verified in the browser in both themes with the geometry measured. No app code touched; the answer is logged into both tasks that were waiting on it. Scripts/test.sh green (6534 tests). Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-14-clamped-range-rule.json.
